summary: Over two iterations, the score improved from 86.951 to 87.162 (+0.211) on a Steiner-tree-like network optimization problem. Three stacking techniques were validated: perturbed MST restarts (+0.082), relay reassignment, and degree-3 hub insertion (+0.129 combined). The remaining improvable gap is small (~1.3 points across 4 test cases), while ~11.5 points are structurally unrecoverable due to relay scarcity on tests 1 and 2.
key_points: Score progression: iter-0 baseline → iter-1 (86.951) → iter-2 (87.162). All gains confirmed via ablation: perturbed restarts contribute 39% of improvement, post-processing (relay reassignment + degree-3 hub insertion) contributes 61%.

6 of 10 test cases are either at perfect score (tests 4,6,7,9 = 10.0 each) or structurally capped by too few relays (tests 1,2 = 6.987 + 1.475). Only tests 3, 5, 8, 10 have remaining headroom totaling ~1.3 points.
Dead ends identified: non-adjacent relay insertion, edge-swap with unused relays, Prim-based perturbation, and screening+selective build all produced zero improvement over the current approach.

Next iteration should investigate: (a) Steiner tree local search (3-opt, edge relocation) for more aggressive topology changes on tests 3/8, (b) randomized greedy insertion order to escape local optima, (c) alternative perturbation noise distributions. Diminishing returns are likely — the maximum possible gain is ~1.3 points.

Risk: the time-limited perturbation loop is sensitive to CPU speed. Under contention, fewer trials run and the score can drop to ~77 (one test case likely hits the 10s TLE). The algorithm should add a safety fallback that preserves the best-so-far solution even if later trials time out.
